newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Veba dismisses talk of deal with BT.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Veba dismisses talk of deal with BT.

text.p: German utility Veba AG on Thursday sought to play down speculation that it was in talks about strategic cooperation with British Telecom Plc after it confirmed the heads of their companies met this week.

The news comes just days after BT competitor Cable and Wireless Plc bailed out of its alliance with Veba and follows statements from Veba officials that the company was actively seeking an international partner to fill the gap.

Commenting on a report in the daily Berliner Zeitung, a Veba spokeswoman said the company's chairman Ulrich Hartmann met on Tuesday with Ian Vallance, the chairman of British Telecom Plc, but denied they talked about cooperation.
"Such speculation is complete nonsense," Veba spokeswoman Marie-Luise Wolff told Reuters.

"Hartmann and Vallance know each other from earlier times and get together frequently for personal reasons," she said, adding: "But you cannot therefore draw the conclusion that British Telecom is the international telecommunications partner that Veba has been looking for."
A host of some of Germany's biggest companies have teamed up with foreign partners to challenge monopoly Deutsche Telekom when the telecommunications market is opened to full competition next year.
The Berliner Zeitung reported on Thursday that Hartmann and Vallance had met to discuss cooperation that could lead to BT leaving its alliance with utility Viag AG.
BT has declined to comment on the report.
British Telecom and Viag were awarded Germany's fourth digital cellular telephone licence on February 4.
The BT-Viag group is widely considered the weakest of three major alliances forming in Germany to challenge monopoly Deutsche Telekom when markets are opened to competition next year.
The newspaper report said BT was "more than dissatisfied" with its alliance with Viag.
At a news conference in Munich last week, BT global operations director Alfred Mockett gave no indication of any such dissatisfaction.
"We have seen a lot of doing and undoing of partnerships recently," he said in a clear reference to the departure last of RWE AG from the BT-Viag alliance to team up with Veba.
"But in all respects our partnership (with Viag) is doing well," he said.

Veba recently sealed its telecoms joint venture with utility RWE AG, which is called O.TEL.O, and said it was in talks with several international companies to replace the departing Cable and Wireless.

Veba and RWE's alliance has begun to look a bit pale compared to the activities of competitor Mannesmann AG, which on Wednesday won a stake in the telecoms business of French railway SNCF through its Cegetel alliance with British Telecom.
